# CLIProxyAPI extraction: the v8 configuration shape

> **Last verified:** 2026-10-22 — CPA 8.0.38 custom YAML decoders are probed
> through yaml.v3; the shared `goTestExtract` runs the extractor over the
> patched `src`; z.ai vendor defaults are extracted from pinned official docs
> into the same owner facts and checked by the owner regenerator.

## Why reflection also needs the v8 tables

`extract/z-ai-sources.json` pins official Markdown documents by content hash
(accessed 2026-10-22). `extract/z-ai.py` parses the overview's chat API table,
Claude Code's JSON environment example, and the quick start's Python AST for the
two base URLs. Featured/Text Models tables require a known chat reference on
every model row; image, tool and agent sections are explicitly excluded. Unknown
sections or references, missing tables, ambiguous URLs, malformed tier bullets,
or a tier pointing outside the catalog fail extraction. The fixtures exclude
prose-only model mentions and image models.

The Claude Code page's explicitly labeled default tier bullets are parsed as
prose (the regex tier: no executable mapping or structured source exists). Later
manual JSON examples disagree with those bullets; the extractor selects the
explicit defaults, and its fixture preserves that distinction. Endpoint examples
are checked separately: identical URLs may repeat, conflicting values fail. All
three tiers must be present, so a changed or unclassified tier fails. These
facts do not alter harness environment variables.

Refresh the three source hashes after reviewing the official documentation, then
run the existing owner regeneration command:
`nix run .#checks.x86_64-linux.cliproxyapi-extracted.passthru.regenerate`.
`cliproxyapi-extracted` joins the config and vendor extraction and checks their
shared committed facts through `mkOwnerCheck`.

`v8Paths` contains relocated paths, not a schema. Fields already at their v8
paths, such as `routing.*` and `models.*`, have no relocation entry. Upstream
key families also change shape through `v8KeyFamilies` and `sharedKeyFields`.
Reading only the relocation table or only the reflected structs loses part of
the configuration.

`extract/config_test.go` is copied into the pinned source's `internal/config`
package so it can read those unexported tables. It reflects every YAML-tagged
`Config` field, rewrites legacy prefixes through `v8Paths` and `v8StructPaths`,
and retains unchanged paths whose roots `v8AllowedRoots()` accepts. Every
relocated current path must appear in the result or extraction fails. Scalar
roots accepted by `v8AllowedRoots()` but absent from the structs, including
`config-version`, take their key and type from the canonical template.

An upstream key family becomes `api-keys.<family>[]` groups holding `name` and
`keys`; `base-url` and `sharedKeyFields` also appear at group level. OpenAI
compatibility keeps its group struct with `api-key-entries` renamed to `keys`.
The v8 group loader does not read `auth-index`, so those fields are omitted.

## Measured data

The package's `passthru.extracted` is `lib/extracted`'s `goTestExtract`: it
copies `package.src`, the `applyPatches` tree, so the facts include what
`patches/key-allowlist.patch` adds to the config schema. It also copies the
package's `goModules`, installs the extractor test beside the shared
`lib/extracted/go/nat_shared_test.go` (node types, the field walk, the output)
and runs it with the package's Go toolchain. `GOPROXY=off`,
`GOFLAGS=-mod=vendor` and `GOTOOLCHAIN=local` keep extraction offline. The
YAML-specific typing (durations, `yaml.Node`, decoder probes) stays here.

Each node holds its measured `type`, its field's Go doc `description` parsed
with `go/parser`, and the `template` comment at the same path in
`config.example.yaml`. Path grammar uses `.` between keys, `[]` for a list
element and `.<name>` for a map value. Every ancestor of a node is a node: v8
sections that no Go struct declares (`server`, `access`, `upstream`, ...) are
`object` nodes carrying the template's section comment. A key the template sets
with no node fails extraction, except below an `any` node. Structs that flatten
into the same mapping join their descriptions; conflicting leaves fail
extraction. A type with a custom YAML decoder is typed by probing that decoder
through yaml.v3: try the scalar `true`, then the sequence `[]`, stopping at the
first success, which makes it `any`. Only if both reject, decode the mapping
`{}`; acceptance makes it an `object` whose reflected fields are its children,
as for a plain struct. Rejection fails extraction with the path, Go type and
probe. `credentials.concurrency` and `oauth.providers.codex.live-media-relay`
decode into plain structs and are `object`;
`multimedia.disable-image-generation` reads `true` and `plugins.configs.<name>`
keeps any YAML subtree, so both are `any`. An `any` struct still retains its
known child fields: the mapping form of `plugins.configs.<name>` has the
measured `enabled` and `priority` fields.

The raw has one `config` tree. `extracted/facts.json` declares it as an opaque
`object` because its keys contain dots, with one Linux measurement because the
configuration shape is host-independent. Shared `lib/extracted` owns loading,
platform carrying and regeneration. The reconciliation reader consumes the
declared object directly.

## Hand annotations

`extract/annotations.json` supplies reasons for credential-bearing config paths.
It contains descriptions of credentials, never credential values.
`extract/rules.nix` reconciles these rows against `config` through the shared
facts loader and `reconcile`.

A `*` pattern matches one key made of letters, digits, `_` or `-`, allowing a
single row such as `api-keys.*[].keys[].api-key` to cover every family. A stale
literal or pattern fails, overlapping rows fail, and a new credential-shaped
string path requires a reason. The shared classifier is
`lib/redact/classify.nix`.

## Checks and updates

`cliproxyapi-extracted` compares the fresh extraction with the committed facts
and checks annotation reconciliation. Regenerate from the repository root:

```bash
nix run .#checks.x86_64-linux.cliproxyapi-extracted.passthru.regenerate
```

The package exposes `passthru.extracted`. Its update script calls the shared
`regenCommand` through `mkGoUpdateExtract.extraAfter`, after repairing the Go
floor and vendor hash, so a release bump carries its new configuration shape
before publication.

# CLIProxyAPI front gate (cpa-gate)

> **Last verified:** 2026-10-23 — the gate refuses non-canonical tool types,
> checks call bodies, filters five CPA listing shapes and detail responses,
> reports listing health, and checks Responses websocket messages; no module
> option enables it.

**cpa-gate is NOT a security boundary, and nothing wires it in yet.** A harness
that runs under the same uid as the gate can read the policy file, which holds
every client key and every internal key, and can read CLIProxyAPI's own config
and logins. It becomes a boundary only once each harness has its own VM or uid.

## What it is

A Caddy HTTP handler, `http.handlers.cpa_gate`, meant to sit in front of
CLIProxyAPI (CPA). It admits a request only when it carries exactly one known
client key on an allowed route, and replaces that key with the entry's internal
key, so CPA applies its key allowlist to the principal the gate chose. The Go
module is `src/cpa-gate` (module path `cpagate`, never fetched); the binary is
Caddy's own `main` plus one import.

`lib/gate.nix` renders the Caddyfile from shared pieces. Only the listing paths
have a downstream `reverse_proxy`; a second loopback site serves
`cpa_gate_health`.

## Policy file

`CPA_GATE_POLICY` carries the policy file's **path**, never a key. The `*`
matcher is required: Caddy takes a first argument that starts with `/` as a path
matcher. A key in a Caddyfile `{$VAR}` would be spliced in before parsing, an
unset one becomes an empty string, and the adapted config holds the value in
clear. The file is JSON:

```json
{
  "entries": [
    {
      "name": "codex",
      "key": "<client key>",
      "internal": "<internal key>",
      "apis": ["responses"],
      "models": ["gpt-6-sol"],
      "hostedTools": {}
    }
  ]
}
```

`Provision` fails on an empty `entries` list (health would report OK while
serving nothing), empty or duplicate entry names (health is keyed by name),
empty keys, `apis` or `models`, unknown API routes or policy fields, duplicate
client keys, a client key equal to an internal key, and trailing JSON. Errors
name entries and fields, never values; entry names are public metadata, since
`/-/health` returns every one to any loopback caller without a credential.
Client keys remain in memory only as SHA-256 digests, scanned with constant-time
comparisons. Each `hostedTools` type declares implied models inside its entry's
set; an empty map denies every hosted tool.

## Requests

1. **Authentication.** CPA reads a key from `Authorization`, `X-Goog-Api-Key`,
   `X-Api-Key`, `?key=` and `?auth_token=`
   (`internal/access/config_access/provider.go`). The gate counts every value of
   all five: exactly one is allowed, so two carriers, a repeated header and a
   repeated query key are refused. `Authorization` must be `Bearer <key>`, with
   the scheme in any case, one separator space, and then the exact configured
   key. An unparsable query is refused here too.
2. **Route.** Method and path match the table in `gate/routes.go` exactly, and
   the path must carry no escaping Go would not produce (`RawPath` empty). So
   `//`, dot segments, a trailing slash, case variants and `%2F` miss. The
   entry's `apis` must admit the route, and the query may hold only the route's
   own keys, once each, besides the carriers.
3. **Rewrite.** On every route but the two websocket ones, `Connection` and
   `Upgrade` are deleted, because `reverse_proxy` relays an upgrade on any
   route. Then all five carriers go and `Authorization: Bearer <internal>` is
   set.

| `apis`      | Routes                                                                                                               | Query                        |
| ----------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------- |
| any         | `GET /v1/models`, `GET /v1/models/{id}`                                                                              | `client_version` on the list |
| `anthropic` | `POST /v1/messages`, `POST /v1/messages/count_tokens`                                                                | `beta`                       |
| `chat`      | `POST /v1/chat/completions`                                                                                          | none                         |
| `gemini`    | `GET /v1beta/models`, `GET /v1beta/models/{name}`                                                                    | none                         |
| `responses` | `POST` `responses` and `responses/compact`, `GET responses` (websocket), each under `/v1/` and `/backend-api/codex/` | none                         |

Calls forward after a strict body check. The gate caps wire and decoded bodies
at 32 MiB, accepts JSON with absent/`identity`/`gzip`/`zstd` encoding, and
forwards the exact decoded bytes with `Content-Encoding` removed. It checks the
top-level `model` with CPA's gjson version, every model-like name at any depth,
and hosted tools against `hostedTools`. Tool declaration types must be lowercase
and have no surrounding whitespace, even when the policy grants the raw
spelling. Top-level `input[].type` values must have no surrounding whitespace
before call suffix checks: CPA trims them when interpreting hosted history.
Canonical dated and preview tool types still require their exact policy grants.
The gate refuses duplicate or escaped directive names, invalid UTF-8, lone
surrogates, non-ASCII names outside client data, trailing values and nesting
beyond 128 levels. Only schemas at `tools[].input_schema`, `tools[].parameters`,
`tools[].function.parameters`, `text.format.schema`,
`response_format.json_schema.schema`, and `output_format.schema`, plus client
tool arguments at their structural positions, are exempt from model checks.

The two Responses websocket routes terminate both connections with
gorilla/websocket v1.5.3 and no compression. Each client text message is
reassembled up to 32 MiB and checked with the same strict gjson v1.18.0 reader.
The first needs a model; later messages may inherit it. Every supplied model is
checked, including interrupt messages. Top-level model values with surrounding
whitespace are refused even if literally in the set: CPA trims them. Accepted
bytes, upstream text/binary messages and both directions of ping/pong/close
controls relay unchanged. Application messages with invalid JSON/UTF-8, excess
size, binary data, non-canonical tool types or disallowed models close the
client with code 1008 and `request refused`, then close the upstream connection.
Gorilla closes transport protocol errors itself. A service restart ends hijacked
sessions by exiting the process.

Listings are parsed by wire shape, never by request header or user agent. Only
exact allowed IDs survive, `first_id`/`last_id` are recomputed, and an object
with a forbidden model directive becomes null (Codex's `upgrade.model`). A
private writer buffers the response, so CPA's interim 1xx headers and trailers
never reach the client. Everything else gets the empty 404: an unknown shape or
envelope field, a paginated listing, non-200, an interrupted or oversized copy,
and a disallowed or missing detail.

`cpa_gate_health` serves `GET /-/health` on a separate loopback site. It starts
failed, then probes each internal principal's `/v1/models` through serving's own
decoder and interpreter, immediately and every 60 seconds. It reports each
entry's `ok` and missing **count**, never model IDs or keys, and refuses any
request carrying a client credential. Logs hold counts only.

## Refusals and logs

- **401**, every authentication failure: `{"error":"Invalid API key"}`, CPA's
  own body for an unknown key (`sdk/access/errors.go`).
- **404**, every route, body, listing, detail or websocket handshake refusal: no
  body, as CPA's gin `NoRoute` answers. Message refusals use the fixed websocket
  close above.

The handler writes refusals itself and returns nil. A returned error would make
Caddy log the whole request. Its own line holds the entry name (`-` before
authentication), the route class, the status and the reason, never a key, a
header or the URI.

Caddy's error log copies the request before any handler runs
(`modules/caddyhttp/server.go`). That copy holds the URI with its query and
every header but the four Caddy redacts, so `?key=`, `X-Api-Key` and
`X-Goog-Api-Key` would reach the journal on any 5xx. The global log block
therefore deletes the whole `request>headers` map and `request>uri`.

## Package and updates

`packages/ai/generic/cpa-gate` builds `cmd/cpa-gate` with `buildGoModule` and
nixpkgs' Caddy version and build tags. `gate.json` pins `goFloor` and
`vendorHash`; nixpkgs and direct updates regenerate it, `go.mod` and `go.sum`,
and `cliproxyapi-gate-pins` checks the version.

**Settled, do not relitigate:** the package is not `caddy.withPlugins`.
`withPlugins` takes a plugin only as `module@version`; it vendors everything
into one fixed-output tree whose hash would move on every gate edit; and its
install check needs a version that a local path lacks.

## Checks

- Go tests run in the package check phase, including a real Caddy copy of
  listings and a test that no log or error carries a key.
- `cliproxyapi-gate-pins`: the Caddy pin, with a wrong-pin control.
- `cliproxyapi-gate-validate`: the real binary validates the rendered Caddyfile
  with a good policy, and refuses a shared key, a missing file and an empty
  path.
- `cliproxyapi-gate-log` (Linux): a running gate, and a site beside it whose
  upstream is down. A key in each carrier reaches neither log. Two controls each
  keep one field and show its unredacted keys; Caddy also redacts Authorization
  itself.

# CLIProxyAPI client-key allowlist

> **Last verified:** 2026-10-22 — the patch applies to CPA 8.0.38 with no fuzz;
> loading rejects duplicate client keys and startup exits 1 on refusal. Hot
> reload can briefly serve a retired config credential under newly widened
> rules, so rotation that also widens access requires a restart or an `ids`
> rule. Named instance client routes derive exact OAuth IDs or API base-URL
> rules.

## Why selection lives in CPA

One CPA instance must bind an authenticated client key to eligible upstream
credentials. A plugin cannot enforce this: if its scheduler fails, unloads, or
returns unhandled, native selection resumes over the full pool. Home mode never
invokes the plugin scheduler. The instance module therefore refuses
`plugins.enabled` with a nonempty allowlist, and CPA refuses Home dispatch while
the allowlist is set. Separate instances were rejected by the operator on
2026-10-21.

CPA's access middleware records the authenticated key for headers, `?key=`, and
`?auth_token=`. The patch uses that recorded principal in candidate selection.
Missing or unknown keys select nothing while the allowlist is set; an absent or
empty allowlist leaves native selection unchanged. A configured key whose
eligible credentials are unavailable gets `auth_not_found`. Model listings still
expose all models. With no upstream credential serving a requested model, CPA
returns `400 unknown provider for model <name>`. Log in with
`cliproxyapi -config <file with auth-dir> -claude-login -no-browser` (or
`-codex-login`), or through Manager Plus; login files are picked up without a
restart.

An entry identifies one client key and grants a list of credential rules. The
client key is a redact reference shared with `access.api-keys[]`. An Instance
owns named client keys and upstream credentials (`ai-proxy.md`); each named
route generates one rule, and Harness selection adds no rules. Write settings
entries by hand only for other clients. A rule requires `provider` and `kind`
(`oauth` or `apikey`); `ids` and `base-urls` narrow it further. Generated
compatibility-provider rules follow CPA's name normalization in
`internal/util/provider.go`. An OAuth credential's ID is its auth-file path
relative to `<stateDir>/auth`, found by listing that directory after CPA login.
A re-login can change the filename; update `credentials.<name>.oauth.authFile`
when it does. A config API key's ID hashes its secret, so use provider and
`base-urls` to address a group through rotation. The settings types and module
refinements are in `cliproxyapi-settings.md`.

The `apikey` kind matches only credentials synthesized from config. A
store-loaded login can temporarily classify as `apikey` from its file or a Meta
refresh before the watcher marks it `oauth`; allowing it through an `apikey`
rule would cross the intended boundary. An OAuth rule can match such a login by
ID once its kind is OAuth. Whoever writes the auth directory controls
file-sourced provider and ID, so high-value OAuth rules should use `ids`.

`base-urls` compares the credential's trimmed `base_url` with each listed URL
after trimming. Provider URL constraints are in `ai-proxy.md`. Scheme, host,
path, case, and trailing slash still matter. A group without an explicit base
URL may have no attribute and cannot match this narrowing; set `base-url`
explicitly for default-endpoint Claude, Gemini, and Interactions groups. A rule
with `base-urls` never matches OAuth, even if an OAuth login carries that
attribute; the instance module refuses that combination. A listed URL absent
from the configured groups is accepted but selects nothing. Key-less OpenAI
compatibility groups have no matching kind and cannot be reached while the
allowlist is set.

## Duplicate keys and load paths

Two entries with the same trimmed client key would merge rules into one
principal and widen access. CPA rejects them by entry index, without logging the
secret. Validation runs after decoding in both `LoadConfigOptional` and
`ParseConfigBytes`: cloud-deploy turns decode errors into an empty config, so
validation inside the decoder would erase a refusal. Initial load (including
cloud-deploy's optional load), hot reload, management writes, and Home pushes
all reach one of these paths. Startup exits 1 before serving; hot reload retains
the previous config and retries a later valid write; management `PUT` answers
422 without writing; a Home push is refused. A caller that constructs `Config`
directly bypasses loading, so the Manager compiles duplicate entries into an
allowlist granting no key any credential. Empty client keys bind no request.

The eligibility predicate covers the legacy candidate loop, scheduler fast path,
retry, and cooldown waits. `SelectAuth` always uses the legacy loop; mixed
`Execute` with a built-in selector exercises the scheduler fast path. Plugin
schedulers receive only surviving candidates. Two 8.0.38 paths bypass that
predicate: Home dispatch, which is refused, and the Antigravity credits
fallback, which checks the allowlist itself. The fallback matters when selection
fails because a client key has no Antigravity rule. Plugin executors and
`host.auth.get` bypass eligibility; this is why enabling plugins must be
refused. `checks/key_allowlist_loops_test.go`, a go/types scan joined to the
auth package, fails on a `range` over `Manager.auths` whose own body calls no
allowlist predicate, unless the function is on its commented exemption list. It
does not see an indexed lookup (`m.auths[id]`), an alias of the map, the map
passed to a helper, or a loop over a copy (`snapshotAuths`, `List`), so a bump
that touches candidate selection still needs source review even if it is green.

## Reload ordering limitation

The watcher publishes the new allowlist before it re-synthesizes config
credentials and asynchronously deletes retired IDs. During that interval an old
credential remains selectable if the new rule grants its provider or base URL.
For example, a reload rotates a Claude key at URL A from secret `sOld` to `sNew`
and grants client K URL A: K may briefly spend on `sOld`. The interval has not
been measured. The secret stays server-side. Narrowing and revocation take
effect first; `ids` rules are safe because the new secret produces a new ID. A
service restart registers credentials before listening and has no such window.
Publishing the allowlist after credential replacement would instead delay
revocation and could fail open, so that reorder was rejected.

## Bumping CPA

The package applies `patches/key-allowlist.patch` to the pinned source with
`-p1 --fuzz=0`; extraction and the Go check read that patched source. Fetch the
version from `sources.json` into scratch, verify its unpacked NAR hash, apply
the patch with `patch --dry-run -p1 --fuzz=0`, and inspect every changed
candidate-selection loop before regenerating the diff. Offset-only moves may
apply; changed context fails. The Go check covers behavior; the loop scan misses
the shapes listed above. Regenerate the extracted settings facts after a schema
change, then run the module assertions and Go check in CI.

<!-- Fragment: packages/cliproxyapi/docs/cliproxyapi-settings.md -->

# CLIProxyAPI typed settings

> **Last verified:** 2026-10-22 — 926 config nodes, including the patched
> `access.key-allowlist`, give the settings type through
> `lib/extracted/options.nix`, with eight refinements and one module assertion
> on the allowlist; the clean render passes native v8 validation and loads
> through CPA 8.0.38's `LoadConfig` in `cliproxyapi-settings`;
> `ai.cliproxyapi.instances` renders it at start, defaults its listener to
> loopback, turns off the unprompted fetches the pinned CPA has a switch for,
> types `server.tls.key` as a secret file, and derives named client keys'
> `access.api-keys` and `access.key-allowlist` entries from named upstream
> routes. Built-in `vendor = "z-ai"` defaults upstream API-key models and APIs
> from pinned official documentation.

`lib/default.nix` exports
`cliproxyapi.{settingsType, render, report, refinements, sample}`. The type is
generated from `config`'s reconciled entries (`extract/rules.nix`), so a path
the extraction adds or drops moves the type with the next regeneration; the
shared rules are in `dev/fragments/extracted/typed-settings.md`.

## Instances

`ai.cliproxyapi.instances.<name>` (`modules/instances.nix`, through
`packages/ai-module/lib/instances.nix`) runs CLIProxyAPI as the service
`cliproxyapi-<name>` on both backends. `port` (8317) fixes `server.port`;
`settings.server.host` defaults to `127.0.0.1` through `mkDefault`, so a
consumer can explicitly override the bind address. `stateDir`
(`<state root>/cliproxyapi/<name>`) fixes `oauth.auth-dir` to `<stateDir>/auth`,
where CLIProxyAPI writes its OAuth logins. The launcher renders the settings to
`config.json` at each start and the run script, inside `stateDir` so the `.env`
and `logs/` CLIProxyAPI resolves against its working directory are its own,
execs `cliproxyapi --config "$CPA_CONFIG"`. CLIProxyAPI's rewrites of its config
reach only that copy and are lost at restart. `ai.proxy.instance` points the
harnesses at an instance by name.

`credentials` and `clientKeys` declare upstream credentials and client access
once on the Instance. Harnesses select
`proxy = {instance = "main"; clientKey = "claude-personal";}`. Shape, a
four-client example, OAuth filename selection and devenv secret references are
in `dev/fragments/ai-proxy/ai-proxy.md`.

For the built-in z.ai vendor, the upstream credential needs only its secret:

```nix
ai.cliproxyapi.instances.main.credentials.zai-api-personal = {
  vendor = "z-ai";
  apiKey.key = redact.file "/run/secrets/zai-api-key";
};
```

`apiKey.apis` defaults to Anthropic-compatible and OpenAI chat-compatible
endpoints, and `apiKey.models` to z.ai's published general API chat catalog.
Override either endpoint's `base-url`, set an API to `null`, or replace `models`
with the subset your upstream credential permits. Check the key classification
and entitlements in z.ai's
[API Key Management Guide](https://docs.z.ai/devpack/notice/api-key-management):
new Standard/Coding Plan keys determine billing across supported endpoints;
older Compatible keys retain endpoint-dependent rules. Standard usage can
consume account balance or usage bundles. The defaults describe the general API,
not a guarantee of account access. Client keys still choose this credential and
its API through `routes`; selecting `api = "chat"` lets CPA translate a Codex
CLI Responses request to chat.

The measured Claude Code tier mapping and timeout remain extraction data. The
existing per-client-key model list carries model IDs for picker rows, without
vendor or tier intent; it cannot safely supply Claude Code environment defaults.

## Unprompted network calls

The pinned CPA starts four background fetchers that need no request and no
credential, each at start and every 3 hours after. The instance module turns off
the ones CPA has a switch for:

| Call                                                                                    | Switch                                                         | Instance default                           |
| --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------ |
| Model catalogs (general, Codex, Devin): raw.githubusercontent.com, models.router-for.me | `--local-model` flag; no setting selects the embedded catalogs | off: the run script passes `--local-model` |
| Management panel: api.github.com and a router-for.me fallback                           | `management.disable-auto-update-panel`                         | off: `mkDefault true`                      |
| Antigravity client version: antigravity-hub-auto-updater Cloud Run manifest             | none                                                           | still on                                   |
| Grok CLI version: registry.npmjs.org                                                    | none                                                           | still on                                   |

To turn one back on, set
`ai.cliproxyapi.instances.<name>.fetchModelCatalogs = true` (the run script
drops `--local-model`) or
`settings.management.disable-auto-update-panel = false`. An explicit
`settings.models.{catalog,codex-catalog,devin-catalog}` source wins over
`--local-model` and is read from its URL or file at the same cadence.

Three more calls happen only on demand and stay: the management panel download
when `/management.html` is requested and the file is missing (any request
triggers it; the download may send a GitHub token from `server.github-token` or
the service environment; `management.disable-control-panel = true` closes it),
the management API's `latest-version` and plugin-store routes, and the public-IP
lookup during an interactive OAuth login. Provider traffic for logins a consumer
added (token refresh, entitlements) is not an unprompted call.

The two calls without a switch send no credential and no request content, only a
GET for a version string, and fail soft to a pinned fallback. Silencing them
takes a patch to CPA, not a setting; that is an open decision.

## Secrets

Every path an `extract/annotations.json` row marks takes a redact reference
only: `access.api-keys[]`, `access.key-allowlist[].api-key`,
`management.secret-key`, `server.github-token`, `requests.proxy-url`, the ICE
server `credential`, and per upstream family the group and key `proxy-url`,
`headers.<name>` and `api-key`. A proxy URL or a header that holds no credential
still takes a reference (`redact.file` or `redact.command`), since the type
cannot tell which values carry one.

`server.tls.key`, the TLS private key file, is a `secretFile` node: it takes a
reference, which the service launcher writes to a 0600 file that the rendered
config names (`dev/fragments/redact/redact.md`, Secret files). `server.tls.cert`
stays a plain path.

`render settings` gives `{ content; secrets; }`: config.yaml as JSON text with
each secret a `{$CLIPROXYAPI_<PATH>}` placeholder, list positions included
(`{$CLIPROXYAPI_API_KEYS_CLAUDE_0_KEYS_0_API_KEY}`). CLIProxyAPI rewrites its
config file at load: it replaces a plaintext `management.secret-key` with its
bcrypt hash and drops conflicting legacy keys. The rendered file must therefore
be a writable copy, never the store path.

## Refinements

Each narrows a measured type using a native constraint in `internal/config/`, or
in the allowlist patch:

- `access.key-allowlist[].credentials[].{base-urls,ids}`:
  `nonEmptyListOf elementType`, the generated string type. The patch reads an
  empty or absent list as no restriction on that dimension, and the renderer
  drops null elements, so an empty list, or `[null]`, would widen the rule to
  every credential of its provider and kind. The type checks definitions, so
  `[(mkIf false "x")]` passes it and merges to `[]`; a module assertion
  (`modules/instances.nix`) refuses any merged empty list. Leave the option
  unset to leave a dimension open.
- `access.key-allowlist[].credentials[].kind`: `enum ["apikey" "oauth"]`; the
  patch matches a rule only when its kind normalizes to a credential kind
  (`normalizeAuthKind`), so any other value would silently allow nothing.
- `client.codex.web-search-result-cache.ttl`: measured `string`, typed as a Go
  duration, because `Validate` in `sdk_config.go` refuses a TTL that is neither
  a duration nor integer seconds; the type admits the duration form only.
- `config-version`: `enum [8]` (`config_v8.go`, "unsupported config-version
  (expected 8)").
- `credentials.in-flight.{snapshot-interval,stale-after,staging-retention}`:
  measured `string`, typed as a Go duration, because `Durations` in
  `credential_in_flight.go` refuses the config when `time.ParseDuration` fails.

The duration refinement checks grammar only; positivity, numeric bounds and
overflow remain native validation. `multimedia.disable-image-generation` keeps
the extracted `any` type, including native string aliases such as `"off"`.

`access.key-allowlist` itself has no refinement. Its elements hold the secret
`api-key`, and the generator refuses a refinement row on a node with a secret
descendant. A module assertion on the merged value (`modules/instances.nix`)
refuses any null entry instead: the renderer drops nulls, so a list of only
nulls, or `[null]`, would render as `[]`, which the patch reads as no allowlist,
and enforcement would be off for every key. An explicit `[]` stays valid.

Cross-field rules stay outside the type: `stale-after` at least three snapshot
intervals, in-flight byte bounds, live media relay port ranges, trusted proxies
as IPs or CIDRs, catalogs as http(s) URLs or absolute paths.

## Check

`cliproxyapi-settings` evaluates `sample` through `settingsType`, with valid
overrides for raw JSON payload params, the Claude client-request-id mode and
cross-field rules. It renders and substitutes dummy secrets, including a proxy
URL with quotes, backslash, colon, hash, brackets, newline and a literal
placeholder. `checks/settings_test.go` validates the clean v8 sample with native
`ValidateV8Config` and rejects an unknown-key control, then injects a
conflicting legacy proxy key and calls `LoadConfig` twice on a writable copy. It
checks both raw payload rules survive, the rewritten file persists the bcrypt
hash and removes the legacy key, every other document value stays equal after
JSON normalization, and the hash and secret remain unchanged on reload.

`module-service-instances-real-daemons` starts the packaged CPA and Manager Plus
through their evaluated Home Manager instance units with runtime dummy secret
files, polls both health endpoints, and checks both listeners are on loopback.
It exists only on Linux. The stand-in instance check separately pins argv,
working directory and state-directory modes.
